features.name: total_cost_score
features.description: Sum of buying price and maintenance cost ordinals; higher means more expensive overall.
features.expected_model_benefit: Allows trees to split on overall affordability in a single threshold.

features.name: cost_imbalance
features.description: Absolute difference between buying and maintenance cost ordinals; captures mismatched pricing profiles.
features.expected_model_benefit: Trees can isolate cars where buying and maintenance diverge sharply.

features.name: utility_score
features.description: Combined practical utility from passenger capacity, luggage capacity, and safety.
features.expected_model_benefit: Single split captures overall practicality of the vehicle.

features.name: is_unsafe
features.description: Indicator that safety rating is at the lowest level (0).
features.expected_model_benefit: Low safety is a strong disqualifier; explicit boolean aids tree splits.

features.name: is_two_person
features.description: Indicator that the car only fits 2 persons (persons == 0).
features.expected_model_benefit: Two-person capacity is a major usability constraint; explicit flag accelerates tree splits.

features.name: high_safety_flag
features.description: Indicator that safety is rated at the top level (2).
features.expected_model_benefit: High safety often required for top evaluations; boolean simplifies splits.

features.name: capacity_safety_interaction
features.description: Product of persons and safety, capturing that both are needed for usability.
features.expected_model_benefit: Nonlinear interaction; zero when either is absent, high when both are high.

features.name: affordability_utility_interaction
features.description: Utility score divided by (1 + total cost); higher means more utility per cost unit.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures value-for-money trade-off useful for ordinal evaluations.

features.name: expensive_flag
features.description: Indicator that both buying and maintenance are in the top two cost tiers (>=2).
features.expected_model_benefit: Identifies uniformly expensive cars in one boolean split.

features.name: premium_practical_flag
features.description: Indicator that the car has high safety, can carry 4+ persons, and has a big boot.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures combinations associated with very good evaluations in a single feature.

features.name: min_practical_dimension
features.description: Minimum among persons, lug_boot, and safety; the weakest practical dimension dominates.
features.expected_model_benefit: Bottleneck logic: if any practical attribute is 0, overall usability is constrained.

features.name: overall_desirability_judgment
features.description: Semantic ordinal grouping of car desirability based on the combination of low cost, sufficient capacity, and safety. Encoded as 0=poor (unsafe or 2-person), 1=mediocre (adequate but expensive or unbalanced), 2=acceptable (balanced utility and cost), 3=excellent (low cost, high utility, high safety).
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a coarse ordinal bucket trees can split decisively without exploring many feature combinations.
